notes: SHS / RHS cope cut-backs: a tube with a wall cut back at its end now gets a proper toolpath. The cut across the coped wall wraps into the corners, and each side wall is one joined cut - along the tab, through its corner chamfer and across the end - with the torch held square to the flat and riding the corner radius at height, never rolling round it and never closer than 2 mm to the steel. These cuts start from the bar end where there is one, and every cut on a wall is finished before the torch moves to the next wall. Square tube ends can be cut face by face (Per Face, a machine setting) with a short lead-out past each corner. Every pierce on a tube end cut or mitre gets a lead-in that follows the cut round the corner (RHS pierce distance and angle in settings, 20 mm at 80 degrees), and only where there is steel to pierce. Editor: a cope deeper than the wall on a tube no longer breaks the part, and tab corner chamfers run out through the corner radius. Import: whole-millimetre files no longer leave a mitred I-beam flange slightly long or turn a cope corner radius into stray arcs; a flange coped flush to the web on an I-beam now gets its toolpath; layout lines drawn off the steel are listed in Import Check. Simulation: steel texture toggle, auto camera for recordings, laser HOME button.
